Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Silhouette 0.9.7

Scoring a given partition

  • Silhouette(), softSilhouette(), cerSilhouette(), dbSilhouette() and calSilhouette() gain a cluster argument for scoring a partition produced elsewhere (for example, by hierarchical clustering). When clust_fun is used, cluster may name the label component of its output (e.g. cluster = "cluster" for ppclust::fcm()). The argument follows ..., so it must be named.
  • Labels now follow one rule: cluster if supplied, otherwise the largest membership in prob_matrix, otherwise the closest cluster in prox_matrix. The exception is the probability density silhouette (PDS, prob_type = "pd"), which assigns each observation to its largest density, as in its definition (Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika, 2024). The neighboring cluster is the closest other cluster in the proximity matrix used.

Behavior changes

  • calSilhouette() scores the same partition in every row except the PDS rows (see above). Previously its crisp and median distance-based rows ignored prob_matrix and used nearest-center labels.
  • softSilhouette(prob_type = "pd") assigns each observation to its largest density for every average, so the PDS lies in [0, 1] as defined. Previously fuzzy averaging used the largest membership instead, which gave negative widths.
  • The exponent a of the fuzzy weights may now be 0 (every weight is then 1 and the fuzzy average equals the crisp average), as in Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024); negative values are rejected.
  • In Silhouette() with prob_matrix, the neighbor is now the closest other cluster in prox_matrix (it was the second largest membership).
  • The fuzzy weights are now the gap between the two largest memberships, as defined by Campello and Hruschka (2006), for every function; they no longer depend on the labels.
  • extSilhouette() no longer rounds ext_sil_width and avg_sil_width to four decimals; the new print method shows four decimals.

Numerical robustness

  • dbSilhouette(): a zero neighboring membership (for example, an underflowed posterior probability) no longer makes every other width zero. Such observations get width 1, the other widths are scaled by the largest finite log ratio, and a warning reports how many there were. When the largest log ratio is below sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), the widths are set to 0 with a warning instead of magnifying rounding error. Equal memberships give width 0.
  • softSilhouette(prob_type = "nlpp"): zero probabilities (infinite -log) no longer give NaN widths or a neighbor equal to the assigned cluster.
  • All width functions: two equal proximities, including two zero distances, give width 0 rather than NaN; infinite proximities give widths of 1 or -1.
  • Input checks are shared by all functions: matrices must be numeric with at least two columns and no NA/NaN (+Inf is allowed in prox_matrix, -Inf is not); negative proximities are rejected (they would give widths outside [-1, 1]); membership rows must be non-negative and sum to 1 within sqrt(.Machine$double.eps); prob_matrix must have the same dimensions as prox_matrix; cluster must hold column numbers.
  • A fuzzy average whose weights are all zero now gives a warning (the average is NaN).

Other improvements

  • extSilhouette() gains a weights argument: "size" (default, as before), "equal", or a numeric vector of user weights. dim_table gains a weight column with each mode’s share, and the result has print() and format() methods.
  • Summaries requested with print.summary = TRUE (and summary()) are reported with message() only, so they can be suppressed with suppressMessages().
  • cerSilhouette(print.summary = TRUE) reported its method as “db”; it now reports “certainty”.
  • plotSilhouette() labeled the legend incorrectly when a cluster was empty.
  • Error messages about prob_matrix no longer refer to prob_type = 'pd' when it was not used.
  • New argument clust_args (a list) in every width function and calSilhouette(). Arguments passed through ... are matched partially against the function’s own arguments first, so m = 3 meant for the fuzzifier of ppclust::fcm() was taken as method; pass such arguments as clust_args = list(m = 3). clust_fun may also be a string of the form "pkg::fun".
  • plotSilhouette(palette = ) keeps the summary legend (the palette used to replace it), a numeric linetype of 0 is accepted as documented, and objects from cluster or factoextra without silhouette information give a clear error.
  • Negative proximities are now an error: they gave widths outside [-1, 1], which summary() and plot() then rejected with a misleading message. That message now points to is.Silhouette(strict = TRUE).
  • extSilhouette() warns when the modes differ in proximity type, method or averaging, and checks for empty objects before computing their averages.
  • The line listing the object’s attributes after print.summary = TRUE is gone.
  • dplyr and lifecycle are no longer imported; inst/CITATION takes the version from the package metadata.

Documentation

  • The help pages describe what each width measures, the labeling rule, tie handling (the first column wins), the row-sum tolerance, when widths can be negative, and why the "medoid" normalization keeps its name although it applies equally to centroids.
  • ?calSilhouette explains which rows are monotone transformations of each other, which coincide in special cases, and which are genuinely different, and lists its actual return columns.
  • Corrected the fuzzy weight formula and the description of nlpp (non-negative, not non-positive).
  • Roxygen markdown is enabled, so bold text and lists in the help pages render properly.
  • ?plotSilhouette cites factoextra::fviz_silhouette(), whose design the plot follows.
  • The help pages use the names of Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024): PACS, PPS, NLPPS and PDS (softSilhouette()), CeS (cerSilhouette()) and DBS (dbSilhouette()), and ?softSilhouette gives the PDS in terms of component densities (for a mixture, gamma/pi-hat = f_k/f).
  • The help pages describe how the number of clusters is read from these widths: the reverse elbow drop of the average for the probability-based widths and local maxima for the DBS, with the result depending on the algorithm, the width and the averaging.
  • New tests cover zero distances and probabilities, ties, K = 2, singleton and empty clusters, NA/Inf input, similarity versus dissimilarity input, supplied labels, objects from other packages, and the exact identities between widths (PAC and medoid; fuzzy c-means memberships and distances; squared distances).

Performance Optimizations

  • Fully vectorized core silhouette computation algorithms (Silhouette, dbSilhouette, cerSilhouette).
  • Replaced slow row-wise apply() and order() sorting routines with highly optimized, C-implemented max.col() and matrix-based masking.
  • Replaced row-wise for loops for calculating silhouette widths and weights with vectorized matrix-index extraction and element-wise arithmetic, yielding dramatic speedups for large datasets.

Documentation

  • Replaced the single long vignette with four shorter ones: vignette("Silhouette") (getting started), vignette("soft-clustering") (widths from membership and posterior probabilities), vignette("interpreting-widths") (relation to the classical silhouette, ranges and valid comparisons) and vignette("multiway") (extended silhouette for block clustering, with a worked double k-means example).
  • Added three articles to the package website: silhouette plots for results from this and other packages, a case study comparing soft clusterings of thyroid patients, and a comparison with other packages that includes measured timings and memory use. The scripts that produce the timings are in data-raw/benchmarks.
  • The vignettes now state that the number of clusters is chosen where the silhouette average is largest, that the rows of calSilhouette() are on different scales and should not be compared with each other, and that simplified averages are not comparable with classical ones or with thresholds published for them.
  • Vignettes no longer attach proxy (which masks stats::dist()), and they skip their code with a message when a suggested package is not installed.
  • Removed the prebuilt vignette files from inst/doc.

Silhouette 0.9.6 (October 2025)

CRAN release: 2025-10-15

New Features

  • Introduced new functions:

  • getSilhouette()
    Constructs a Silhouette class object directly from user-provided components without performing silhouette calculations. Allows users to build Silhouette objects when they already have cluster assignments, neighbor clusters, silhouette widths, and optional weights.

  • is.Silhouette()
    Tests whether an object is of class “Silhouette” with optional strict validation. Checks both class inheritance and expected structure including required columns, attributes, and value ranges.

  • cerSilhouette()
    Computes certainty silhouette widths for soft clustering using maximum posterior probabilities. Provides an alternative evaluation method for fuzzy clustering algorithms with support for crisp, fuzzy, and median averaging.

  • dbSilhouette()
    Computes density-based silhouette widths using log-ratios of posterior probabilities based on Menardi (2011) method. Offers normalized silhouette evaluation for soft clustering with enhanced discrimination between cluster assignments.

  • calSilhouette()
    Computes all available silhouette indices from the package functions and returns a comparative summary data frame. Automatically calculates crisp, fuzzy, and median silhouette values across different methods including proximity-based (medoid, pac), soft silhouette variations (pp_pac, pp_medoid, nlpp_pac, nlpp_medoid, pd_pac, pd_medoid), and probability-based methods (cer, db). Supports direct matrix input or clustering function output for streamlined comparative analysis.

Improvements

  • Extended existing functions to support median-based silhouette calculations as an alternative to mean-based computations.
  • Added new average attribute for existing Silhouette class supporting “crisp”, “fuzzy”, and “median” options.
  • Enhanced clustering evaluation capabilities with density-based and certainty-based statistical measures.
  • Updated documentation to reflect new median calculation options and soft clustering methods.
  • Enhanced calSilhouette() to compute all combinations of softSilhouette() methods (pp, nlpp, pd) with both pac and medoid approaches, providing comprehensive comparative analysis across 11 different silhouette computation methods.

Updated Dependencies

  • Imports: dplyr, ggplot2, ggpubr, lifecycle, methods, stats
  • Suggests: proxy, ppclust, blockcluster, cluster, factoextra, drclust

Silhouette 0.9.5 (August 2025)

  • Improved documentation:
    • Updated README.md and DESCRIPTION fields.
    • Fixed an example in the vignettes for clarity.
  • Added lifecycle badges to all exported functions.

Silhouette 0.9.4 (July 2025)

CRAN release: 2025-07-30

CRAN Suggested Corrections

  • Clarified the description of the PAC (Probability of Alternative Cluster) method in the documentation by citing the original authors (Author, Year).
  • Removed usage of installed.packages() from the package code and replaced it with a more robust and CRAN-compliant approach, following suggested practices.
  • All user-facing functions now include the argument print.summary, which controls whether summary details are printed. This argument behaves similarly to if (verbose) cat(...) and now defaults to FALSE.
  • Messages using message() are included in example sections to suggest installation of optional packages (e.g., ppclust, blockcluster). These packages are not called directly, but their outputs are used in examples. This is done to guide users without violating CRAN’s policy on requiring packages in examples.
  • Removed the license file as suggested.

Silhouette 0.9.3 (July 2025)

  • Removed Citation file from inst folder and added WORDLIST in it.
  • Modified Description and Title in DESCRIPTION file.

Silhouette 0.9.2 (July 2025)

Initial Stable Release

The first stable release of the Silhouette package, offering tools to compute and visualize silhouette widths for evaluating clustering quality. It supports both crisp and soft clustering outputs, along with multi-way clustering (e.g., biclustering).

Key Features

  • Silhouette()
    Computes silhouette widths using proximity matrices (dissimilarity or similarity). Supports "medoid" and "pac" normalization methods, and fuzzy silhouette calculation via membership probabilities.

  • softSilhouette()
    Tailored for soft clustering. Transforms membership probabilities into proximity measures (posterior probabilities, negative log-probabilities, or raw distributions) before silhouette computation.

  • extSilhouette()
    Extends silhouette analysis to multi-way clustering (e.g., biclustering or triclustering) by aggregating silhouette widths across modes, weighted by observation counts.

  • plotSilhouette()
    Creates detailed silhouette plots using ggplot2, with options for grayscale themes, cluster-wise summaries, and labeled observations. Compatible with outputs from Silhouette, softSilhouette, and popular packages like cluster and factoextra.

  • summary.Silhouette()
    Summarizes silhouette results, including average silhouette widths per cluster and overall summary statistics.

Dependencies

  • Imports: dplyr, ggplot2, ggpubr, methods
  • Suggests: proxy, ppclust, blockcluster, cluster, factoextra
